facts.statement: Acheroraptor was scientifically described in 2013 by Canadian paleontologists David Evans, Derek Larson, and Philip J. Currie.
facts.quote: It was described by Canadian paleontologists David Evans, Derek Larson, and Philip J. Currie in 2013.

facts.statement: The genus Acheroraptor contains only one species, A. temertyorum, which is based on an isolated maxilla with teeth.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, A. temertyorum, based on an isolated maxilla with teeth.

facts.statement: Fossils of Acheroraptor were first collected on 28 August 2009 by commercial collectors in the Hell Creek Formation, 45 km southwest of Jordan, Montana.
facts.quote: Fossils of Acheroraptor were first collected on 28 August 2009 by commercial fossil collectors in sediments of the Hell Creek Formation in a site 45 km southwest of Jordan, Garfield County, Montana in the western United States.

facts.statement: The discovered remains include a complete right maxilla (ROM 63777) and an assigned dentary (ROM 63778), both housed at the Royal Ontario Museum.
facts.quote: The remains found consisted of a complete right maxilla with several maxillary teeth, cataloged as ROM 63777 at the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto, and an assigned dentary, ROM 63778.

facts.statement: The Royal Ontario Museum purchased the Acheroraptor fossils from a private collector.
facts.quote: The ROM subsequently purchased the two fossils from a private collector.

facts.statement: A 2020 abstract reported new findings regarding the holotype locality of Acheroraptor, abbreviated as AHL.
facts.quote: An abstract from the 2020 Canadian Society of Vertebrate Paleontology Meeting reported new findings on Acheroraptor and its holotype locality (abbreviated as AHL).

facts.statement: Postcranial material, including three manual phalanges and a claw, was later assigned to Acheroraptor.
facts.quote: Additionally, postcranial material consisting of three manual phalanges and a claw were assigned to Acheroraptor.

facts.statement: Acheroraptor lived in present-day Montana during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Acheroraptor (meaning "underworld thief") is an extinct genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in present-day Montana in the United States during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The fossils come from the upper part of the Hell Creek Formation, dating to the latest Maastrichtian stage immediately before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: The strata where these fossils were unearthed derives from the upper part of the Hell Creek Formation, dating to the latest Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, immediately prior to the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

facts.statement: Palynological data indicates the Acheroraptor holotype locality comes from the lower-middle half of the Hell Creek Formation, not the upper half.
facts.quote: Instead of belonging to the upper half of the Hell Creek Formation, the AHL actually comes from the lower-middle half based on palynological data.

facts.statement: Acheroraptor was initially described as a mid-sized dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: In its initial description, Acheroraptor was described as a "mid-sized" dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: The lead author suggested Acheroraptor was similar in size to Deinonychus, estimated at 3.3–3.4 meters long and weighing 60–73 kg (or up to 100 kg).
facts.quote: The lead author of its description stated that it was similar in size to Deinonychus, which was estimated to be around 3.3 - 3.4 m long and weighed up to 60 - 73 kg or even 100 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a nearly complete right maxilla with several teeth, showing minor damage and a missing section of the jugal ramus.
facts.quote: The holotype includes a nearly complete right maxilla and several teeth, with minor crushing, cracks, and missing a small section of the jugal ramus.

facts.statement: A slight chin is present at the apex of the dentary, which is much weaker than that of Velociraptor.
facts.quote: At the apex of the dentary is a slight "chin", one much weaker than that observed in the related Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Acheroraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of theropods found in the Americas, Antarctica, Asia, and Oceania during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Acheroraptor belonged to the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of theropods that existed during the Cretaceous in the Americas, Antarctica, Asia, and Oceania.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Acheroraptor as a member of the clade containing Eudromaeosauria and Microraptorinae, confirming its placement in Dromaeosauridae and possibly Eudromaeosauria.
facts.quote: Acheroraptor was recovered as a member of the clade containing Eudromaeosauria and Microraptorinae, confirming its referral to the Dromaeosauridae, and possibly to Eudromaeosauria.

facts.statement: Two 2020 studies classified Acheroraptor as a basal member of the subfamily Velociraptorinae, extending the known range of this group to North America.
facts.quote: In two 2020 studies, Acheroraptor was classified as a basal member of the subfamily Velociraptorinae which, along with taxa like Dineobellator or even Deinonychus, would extend the known range of the group to North America.

facts.statement: Analysis suggests Acheroraptor had relatively weak jaws adapted for rapid, slashing bites on smaller prey, similar to Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: An examination of the bite force of Acheroraptor suggests that like members of the Velociraptorinae, it was equipped with relatively weak jaws for inflicting rapid, slashing bites on smaller prey.

facts.statement: Acheroraptor fossils were first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, located in modern-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Acheroraptor was first found in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans parts of modern-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.

facts.statement: The Hell Creek Formation environment where Acheroraptor lived was warm, humid, and swampy with maritime to subtropical conditions.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of this region was warm, humid, and swampy environment, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.

facts.statement: Average temperatures in the Hell Creek Formation ranged from 11.3 to 11.6 °C (52.3 to 52.9 °F).
facts.quote: The average temperatures ranged from 11.3–11.6 °C (52.3–52.9 °F).

facts.statement: Cycads and Ginkgo trees were present in the Hell Creek Formation ecosystem.
facts.quote: Cycads and Ginkgo trees were also present.

facts.statement: The rivers and lagoons of the Hell Creek Formation hosted invertebrates, fish, amphibians, and reptiles including turtles, crocodilians, Champsosaurus, and mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Small insects are known from what would have been the swampy forests, while the rivers and lagoons hosted invertebrates (bivalves and ammonites), fish (sharks, hybodonts, gars, and sturgeons), amphibians (frogs and salamanders), and various reptiles (turtles, crocodilians, the choristodere Champsosaurus, and mosasaurs in the coastal, brackish, and freshwater zones).

facts.statement: Diverse small terrestrial mammals and lizards lived alongside early snakes in the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: Small terrestrial mammals and lizards were diverse, living alongside early snakes.

facts.statement: Pterosaurs found in the Hell Creek Formation include the azhdarchid Infernodrakon and an unnamed pteranodontian.
facts.quote: Pterosaurs are represented by the azhdarchid Infernodrakon and an unnamed pteranodontian.

facts.statement: Acheroraptor is one of the geologically youngest known dromaeosaurids, alongside taxa like Dineobellator and Dakotaraptor.
facts.quote: It is one of the geologically youngest dromaeosaurids known, along with taxa like Dineobellator and Dakotaraptor.

facts.statement: Evans, Larson, and Currie (2013) concluded that Acheroraptor was the only dromaeosaurid from the Hell Creek Formation and that teeth previously attributed to Dromaeosaurus and Saurornitholestes actually belonged to it.
facts.quote: Evans, Larson, and Currie (2013) concluded that Acheroraptor was the only dromaeosaurid from the Hell Creek Formation, and that teeth previously referred to Dromaeosaurus and Saurornitholestes actually came from the taxon.

facts.statement: The view that Acheroraptor was the only dromaeosaurid in the Hell Creek Formation was disproven in 2015 with the description of the larger Dakotaraptor.
facts.quote: In 2015, this view was disproven, with the description of Dakotaraptor, a far larger second dromaeosaur from the formation.

facts.statement: While initially thought to come from the upper layer of the Hell Creek Formation, a 2020 abstract suggests Acheroraptor came from the lower layer.
facts.quote: Although initially thought to come from the former, a 2020 abstract suggests Acheroraptor came from the latter.

facts.statement: Acheroraptor belongs to the parent group Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Velociraptorinae

facts.statement: Acheroraptor is classified in the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Acheroraptor is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Acheroraptor lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
